iterations.explanation: Seven orthogonal axes separate behavior structuring, notifications, availability synchronization, operations, pricing, payments, and session security; no previous feedback existed.

clusters.name: Rental Operation Structuring
clusters.description: Architectural patterns for structuring executable rental operations, including where command-based encapsulation applies or is deliberately excluded.

relations.rationale: Authenticated sessions are required to safely authorize rental actions and prevent unauthorized operation execution.

values.label: Command-Based Rental Operations
values.description: Encapsulates rental actions as command objects to organize execution and potentially support queuing, logging, or undo behavior.

values.label: Scoped Command Application
values.description: Limits command usage to rental operations rather than applying it to notification scheduling, preserving responsibility boundaries.

clusters.name: Client Notification Delivery
clusters.description: Client-facing delivery of rental and usage updates, distinguished by notification propagation and asynchronous UI scheduling rather than inventory synchronization.

relations.rationale: Client notifications commonly consume state changes produced by bike availability synchronization.

values.label: Observer-Based Rental Notifications
values.description: Uses observers to notify UI components when rental state changes, keeping client views synchronized with rental activity.

values.label: Asynchronous Notification Scheduling
values.description: Uses asynchronous scheduling when necessary so state-change notifications do not block application processing or degrade UI responsiveness.

values.label: Observer-Based User Updates
values.description: Uses observers to push bike-status and usage-history changes to users and other interested client consumers.

clusters.name: Bike Availability Synchronization
clusters.description: Mechanisms for detecting bike-status changes and refreshing availability data, distinct from delivering broader user notifications.

relations.rationale: Availability changes provide operational state that monitoring dashboards and analytics can consume.
Availability state changes are a direct source of client-facing availability notifications.

values.label: Observer-Based Availability Refresh
values.description: Uses observers to refresh the available-bike list whenever a bike status changes.

values.label: Status-Change Driven Synchronization
values.description: Triggers availability updates directly from bike-status transitions, making state change the synchronization event.

clusters.name: Operational Monitoring and Analytics
clusters.description: Aggregation and interpretation of live bike operations data for dashboards, monitoring, and usage-based operational insight.

relations.rationale: Monitoring and analytics depend on current operational state, including synchronized bike availability and status data.

values.label: Aggregated Operations Dashboard
values.description: Aggregates bike status information into an operational dashboard for centralized visibility.

values.label: Real-Time Operational Monitoring
values.description: Provides live visibility into bike conditions and platform operations.

values.label: Usage Analytics Processing
values.description: Processes usage data to support operational analysis and service optimization.

clusters.name: Rental Pricing Calculation
clusters.description: Architectural strategies for determining rental charges, separate from the mechanisms that execute external payment transactions.

relations.rationale: The calculated rental amount is an input required by payment-provider integration when charging a rider.

values.label: Strategy-Based Pricing Calculation
values.description: Uses a dedicated strategy abstraction to select and vary rental pricing calculation behavior.

values.label: Separated Pricing and Notification Timing
values.description: Keeps notification timing outside pricing calculation, maintaining separation between charge computation and event delivery responsibilities.

clusters.name: Third-Party Payment Integration
clusters.description: Abstraction and decoupling choices for integrating multiple external payment providers while preserving a stable internal payment contract.

relations.rationale: Payment integration requires a computed charge amount from the rental pricing strategy before invoking an external provider.

values.label: Adapter-Based Payment Integration
values.description: Wraps third-party payment providers with adapters so provider-specific interfaces conform to the platform’s internal contract.

values.label: Common Internal Payment Interface
values.description: Exposes a common internal payment interface, insulating rental services from provider-specific APIs and implementation details.

clusters.name: Authenticated Session Protection
clusters.description: Controls for limiting authenticated account exposure over time, distinct from rental behavior, notifications, payments, and operational data processing.

relations.rationale: Session timeout limits the period during which users can access protected rental and payment-related operations.

values.label: Fifteen-Minute Inactivity Timeout
values.description: Automatically logs users out after 15 minutes of inactivity to reduce unauthorized access risk.

values.label: Automatic Idle Logout
values.description: Terminates authenticated sessions automatically after an idle period as an account and privacy protection.

saturation_history.rationale: All relevant open codes are already subsumed by existing taxonomy dimensions. The Command-pattern items map directly to Dimension 1 (Rental Operation Structuring), the observer/asynchronous notification items map to Dimension 2 (Client Notification Delivery), bike availability/status-change refresh items map to Dimension 3 (Bike Availability Synchronization), dashboard/real-time monitoring/analytics map to Dimension 4 (Operational Monitoring and Analytics), pricing strategy and notification-separation map to Dimension 5 (Rental Pricing Calculation), payment integration/interface items map to Dimension 6 (Third-Party Payment Integration), and inactivity timeout/automatic logout map to Dimension 7 (Authenticated Session Protection). No open code introduces a distinct architectural concern outside these existing axes for the CityBike use case.

All relevant open codes are already subsumed by existing taxonomy dimensions. The authentication-related codes map to Dimension 7 (Identity and Data Security), including verification token validity, signup identity/contact collection, password-based authentication, optional location data collection, registration security controls, code delivery channel, and multiple code-expiry variants. The persistence/querying codes map to Dimension 4 (Operational Data and Reporting), specifically repository-based bike persistence, repository-based usage querying, report assembly, and downloadable usage history. The remaining codes about encryption and confidentiality are also covered by Dimension 7. No open code introduces a new architectural axis distinct from the existing security, persistence, reporting, or authentication concerns, so no uncovered concepts remain.
